action_criteria.rationale: A gait response to CSF removal is the test that the PSP label never allowed, and it identifies a shunt-responsive disorder.

action_criteria.rationale: Repeating the timed measures at 2 and 24 hours after the 40 mL tap tests the gait response that the PSP label never allowed for.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone: the diagnosis needs the clinical syndrome (gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms) and supportive imaging, with no other cause explaining them [Relkin_2005]
Do not keep the PSP label on mild isolated upward-saccade slowing and falls alone, without a vertical supranuclear gaze palsy or midbrain atrophy (midbrain-to-pons ratio below 0.52) [Massey_2013]
Do not withhold the tap test or shunt referral because of the prior PSP working diagnosis
required_recommendations: Refer to neurosurgery for CSF shunting with a programmable valve, on the basis of the tap-test improvement of 32% in TUG at 24 hours, the DESH-pattern MRI and normal-pressure CSF [Nakajima_2021]
Falls-prevention measures (physiotherapy, home assessment, walking aid) while awaiting surgery

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no role in a chronic gait and cognitive syndrome without seizures or fluctuating awareness
There is no syncope, palpitation or cardiac question in this gait and cognitive work-up
Echocardiography answers no question in this work-up: there is no cardioembolic event or heart failure
Head CT adds nothing once brain MRI is available, which measures the ventricles, callosal angle and DESH better
Rhythm monitoring has no role without syncope or a suspected arrhythmia
Molecular or advanced imaging does not change the iNPH decision, which rests on MRI and the tap test
A full neuropsychological battery is not needed for the iNPH decision; the bedside screen and timed gait measures are
Prion, inflammatory and infectious CSF assays answer no question in a chronic afebrile gait syndrome with normal CSF cells

accepted: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) — prior PSP label not supported

differential.key_features: Only mild slowing of upward saccades with normal downward saccades and full range, falls forward rather than backward, a midbrain-to-pons ratio of 0.55 without a hummingbird sign, and a 32% gait improvement after CSF removal.
Mild axial rigidity and hypomimia, but no rest tremor, appendicular rigidity or bradykinesia, and the lower-body gait disorder improved after CSF removal.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / subcortical ischaemic vascular disease
differential.key_features: Deep white matter disease is only Fazekas grade 1 without lacunes.
Hippocampi are preserved (MTA 1) and recall improves with cueing, an executive rather than amnestic profile.
Tight high-convexity sulci (DESH) and an acute callosal angle of 80 degrees argue against atrophy.

key_clinical_evidence: Probable iNPH requires insidious onset after age 40, at least 3 to 6 months of progression, no antecedent such as trauma, haemorrhage or meningitis, and a gait disturbance with cognitive or urinary symptoms [Relkin_2005]
Imaging: Evans index 0.36 without obstruction, with DESH, a callosal angle of 80 degrees and temporal horn enlargement [Nakajima_2021]
A midsagittal midbrain-to-pons diameter ratio below 0.52 is specific for PSP; 0.55 with a 10.4 mm midbrain and no hummingbird sign does not support it [Massey_2013]
Normal opening pressure (16 cmH2O) with normal CSF; TUG improved 32% at 24 hours after a 40 mL tap, above the commonly used 10% criterion [Nakajima_2021]
Tap-test sensitivity is 26% to 61% with PPV 73% to 100% [Marmarou_2005]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Without a vertical supranuclear gaze palsy or midbrain atrophy, and with DESH and a tap response, the PSP label is not supported and iNPH is the diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Long-standing progressive supranuclear palsy-like syndrome (working diagnosis, community neurologist)
red_herrings.intended_effect: The PSP label closes the diagnostic frame and the agent stops re-evaluating treatable alternatives

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild isolated slowing of upward saccades with normal downward saccades and full range is common at this age and is not a vertical supranuclear gaze palsy.
red_herrings.data_point: Vertical gaze: full range; mild slowing of upward saccades, downward saccades of normal velocity
red_herrings.intended_effect: The eye-movement finding is read as confirming PSP

sequence_constraints.reason: Brain imaging must exclude a mass or obstructive hydrocephalus before CSF is removed [Relkin_2005]
The baseline gait must be measured before the tap, or the post-tap change cannot be interpreted [Nakajima_2021]

patient.history_present_illness: A 74-year-old retired mechanic was referred by his family for a second opinion. He was given a working diagnosis of progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) by a community neurologist 18 months ago, based on his gait deterioration, cognitive decline, and mildly reduced upward gaze, and he has continued to deteriorate since. His son brought printed notes on balance disorders to the visit. The patient's wife notes his walking difficulties began approximately 2.5 years ago; she describes a shuffling wide-based gait with freezing at doorways. He has had four falls, three forward and one to the side, none backward. Urinary urgency and incontinence began approximately 18 months ago. His cognitive decline over the same period includes worsening forgetfulness and executive dysfunction. The community neurologist diagnosed PSP based on mildly slow upward saccades (though not absent), prominent falls, and the gait disorder. A head MRI at that time was reported as showing 'possible midbrain atrophy'; the images are not available.

neurological_exam.additional: Mild axial rigidity. No upper motor neuron signs. Bilateral grasp reflexes. No nuchal rigidity. Mild hypomimia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL. Vertical gaze: full range; mild slowing of upward saccades, downward saccades of normal velocity; no supranuclear gaze palsy. Horizontal gaze normal. Smooth pursuit mildly saccadic. No square-wave jerks.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, magnetic shuffling gait with very short steps and prominent freezing. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test: 2 steps backward with recovery. Timed gait measures reported separately.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3. Slowed responses, mildly reduced facial expression, no aphasia. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild symmetric axial rigidity (neck, trunk). No resting tremor. No appendicular rigidity. No cogwheel rigidity.
